Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg., cor EDSA Mapagmahal Street, Diliman, Quezon City OFFICE OF THE SECRETARY DILG OPINION NO. 46 S. 2010 April 16, 2010 BONIFACIO M. QUIROG, JR. Secretary to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan Bohol Dear Mr. Quirog: This pertains to your letter-query seeking the opinion of this Department regarding the status of your Provincial Liga ng mga Barangay Federation President and Provincial Councilor League President after they filed their certificate of candidacies for the position of Vice-Governor and Sangguniang Panlalawigan Member, respectively. In reply thereto, please be informed that the issues that you have raised in your letter had already been settled in DILG Opinion No. 5, series of 2010 that any person holding an elective office or position shall not be considered resigned upon the filing of his certificate of candidacy for the same or any other elective office or position (Sec. 4 Comelec Resolution No. 8678, 06 October 2009). Attached herewith is the said DILG Opinion for your ready reference. Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secretary: ATTY. JESUS B. OQUE 1 Director lit Legal Service cc: Director Pedro A. Noval Regional Director-Region VII Sudlan, Lahug, Cebu City Legal:20/corz

Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City OFFICE OF THE UNDERSECRETARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG Opinion No. 05, s. 2010 15 January 2010 VICE-MAYOR RAMON B. ABINUMAN Cawayan, Masbate Dear Vice-mayor Abinuman: This has reference to your earlier letter where you posed the following queries for our resolution, to wit: "I) Is the ABC President having filed his COC, considered automatically resigned? 2) What happens to his privileges and benefits as Ex-Officio Member of the Sangguniang Bayan, such as his earned leave credits? 3) Does the Vice President of the Association automatically assume Mr. Burga's position in the Sangguniang Bayan?" In reply to your first query, allow us first to lay down the pertinent provisions 'of law and its subsequent amendments and modification. To start with, Section 67 of the Omnibus Eleciton Code (BP 881) provides that "Any elective official, whether national or local, running for any office other than the one which he is holding in a permanent capacity, except for President and Vice-President, shall be considered ipso facto resigned from his Office upon filing of his certificate of candidacy. However, this section was later on modified by Section II of Republic Act No. 8436, otherwise known as "An Act Authorizing the Commission on Elections to Use an Automated 1998 National and Local Elections and in Election System in the May II, Subsequent National and Local Electoral Exercises", which provides that "xxx (a) any elective official, whether national or local, running for any office other than the one which he/she is holding in a permanent capacity, except for president and vice-president, shall be deemed resigned only upon the start of the campaign period corresponding to the position for which he/she is running xxx" In a later development, the "Fair Elections Act" (RA 9006) was approved by the President of the Philippines on February 12, 2001, and Section 14 thereof expressly repealed Section 67 of the Omnibus Election Code and also rendered the 3rd paragraph of Section 11 of RA 8436 to be already ineffective. In view of the foregoing turn of events, there is now no law providing for the effects of filing of certificate of candidacy by incumbent elective officials whether running for the same or another office other than the one which he is holding in a permanent capacity.

-2 In line with the above discussion, it bears stressing that the Commission on Elections (COMELEC), pursuant to its power to issue the Rules and Regulations governing the elections, promulgated on 06 October 2009 Resolution No. 8678 pertaining to the Guidelines on the Filing of Certificates of Candidacy (COC) and Nomination of Official Candidates of Registered Political Parties in Connection with the 10 May 2010 National and Local Elections. Section 4 thereof states that: "SEC. 4. Effects of Filing Certificates of Candidacy.—a) b) Any person holding an elective office or position shall not be considered resigned upon the filing of his certificate Of candidacy for the same or any other elective office or position. Section 4(b) thereof pertaining to elective officials is the legal basis on the instant matter unless otherwise abandoned in a later issuance of the Commission or by an act of Congress. Accordingly, the ABC President is not considered resigned from his position as Punong Barangay. Being still a Punong Barangay and ABC President, he is entitled to sit as ex-officio in the Sangguniang Bayan per Section 494 of the Local Government. Having said the foregoing, queries 2 and 3 should not be answered anymore. We hope we have guided you accordingly. Very truly yours, AUSTERE A. PANADERO Undersecretary Ls/17/md Dir. Blandino M. Maceda DILG Region V Legazpi City The Municipal Local Government Operations Officer Cawayan, Masbate
